issues.legal_issue: Expiry of the time allowed for deciding a building-sanction application does not itself create deemed sanction or a right to build.
material_facts: An application for permission to construct additional floors remained undecided beyond the periods set out in the applicable rules and court orders.
The governing enactment and rules required express sanction and did not provide that failure to decide within the specified period would amount to deemed sanction or deemed refusal.
issues.conclusion: The applicant acquired no sanction merely because the application remained undecided after the relevant periods; construction required express approval.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 173 to 175 of the Howrah Municipal Corporation Act and Rule 3 of the Building Rules require sanction before construction, and neither the Act nor the rules creates deemed sanction or deemed refusal on expiry of the decision period. Applying Chet Ram Vashist v. Municipal Corporation of Delhi, failure to decide within a prescribed period does not by itself create a right to claim sanction.

predicates.building_sanction_proceeding: A person sought permission from a public authority to construct or alter a building.
predicates.application_undecided_past_deadline: The authority did not decide the building-sanction application within the period allowed for its decision.
predicates.no_automatic_approval_rule: The governing rules did not make an undecided application automatically approved or rejected after the decision period.

issues.definition: When a building-sanction application remains undecided beyond its decision period and the governing rules do not make silence an approval, construction still requires express approval.

issues.legal_issue: A pending application and a court-ordered deadline for its consideration do not create a vested right to have it decided under superseded building rules.
material_facts: Permission had been granted for construction up to four floors, while the applicant was left free to apply for permission for further floors.
A later court order expressed an expectation that the further application would be decided within a stated period but did not direct that permission be granted.

Before the further application was decided, the building rules were amended and a municipal resolution, approved by the relevant executive body, restricted building heights in specified areas because of limited civic services.
The proposed additional construction was contrary to the restrictions in force when the authority refused permission.
issues.conclusion: The rules in force when sanction is granted or refused govern the application; the applicant had no vested right to sanction under the earlier rules, and the later restrictions applied to the pending application.
issues.legal_principle: The Act and Building Rules regulate construction in the public interest and do not give an applicant a vested right to approval under the rules in force on the application date. A court order allowing an applicant to apply or requiring timely consideration does not direct approval or freeze the applicable rules. Usman Gani J. Khatri v. Cantonment Board and State of West Bengal v. Terra Firma Investment and Trading Pvt. Ltd. establish that building plans are governed by the regulations in force at the time of sanction and that no legal right to approval arises merely from submitting a plan. The restrictions were imposed under Rule 20(3), with the required approval, in response to civic-service concerns; public interest and convenience prevail over a claimed settled expectation.

rule.if: building_sanction_proceeding and application_pending_when_rules_changed and court_order_only_allowed_application_or_required_consideration and new_restrictions_in_force_at_decision

predicates.building_sanction_proceeding: A person sought permission from a public authority to construct or alter a building.
predicates.application_pending_when_rules_changed: The building-sanction application remained pending when the governing construction rules changed.
predicates.court_order_only_allowed_application_or_: A court order allowed the applicant to seek further approval or required the authority to consider the application, without directing that approval be granted.
predicates.new_restrictions_in_force_at_decision: When the authority decided the application, changed rules restricted the proposed construction.
predicates.superseded_rules_do_not_create_entitleme: The applicant has no entitlement to approval under rules that were replaced before the application was decided.

issues.definition: If a building-sanction application is pending when rules change, and a court order only permits or requires consideration of the application, the former rules do not entitle the applicant to sanction once the new restrictions are in force.

issues.legal_issue: A prior court order permitting an application for additional construction does not excuse compliance with requirements for a fresh application and plans.
material_facts: The applicant had received permission to build up to four floors and was told that it could apply for permission for further construction if permissible.
The applicant sought permission for three additional floors, and the authority required fresh plans and supporting documents for the proposed addition.
The building rules required a person making an addition to apply for sanction, and the applicant subsequently supplied the requested material.
issues.conclusion: The prior order did not exempt the applicant from the requirements for a fresh application and plans, and the authority's insistence on those requirements was not a malicious or deliberate attempt to delay the application.
issues.legal_principle: Rules 3 and 4 of the Building Rules prohibit additions without sanction and require a written application for additions to an existing building. An order stating that an applicant is not prevented from applying for further sanction does not displace those requirements.

predicates.building_addition_sanction_proceeding: A person sought permission to add to an existing building.
predicates.prior_court_order_only_permitted_further: A prior court order allowed the applicant to seek further permission but did not itself grant permission for the proposed addition.
predicates.rules_require_fresh_application_for_addi: The governing rules required a fresh application and plans for an addition to an existing building.
predicates.fresh_application_and_plans_required: The proposed addition must be supported by the fresh application and plans required by the governing rules.

issues.definition: When a person seeks approval for an addition and a prior court order only allowed a further application, the person must still provide the fresh application and plans required by the rules.
